Ashkenaz
ash'ke-naz
n. (eldest son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth; a northern kingdom summoned by Jeremiah against Babylon)
From Hebrew 'Ashkenaz, of uncertain derivation. The Chronicler and Jeremiah spell it Ashchenaz in the KJV, the same name in a slightly different transmission; Genesis has Ashkenaz.

Biblical Definition

Ashkenaz is the firstborn of Gomer and so a grandson of Japheth: “And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah” (Gen 10:3). He would be one more name in the northern column but for a single verse in Jeremiah that lifts him into prophecy. Announcing the fall of Babylon, the prophet calls up the armies God has appointed to execute it: “call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; appoint a captain against her” (Jer 51:27). Three northern kingdoms, none of them worshippers of the LORD, are summoned by name as His instruments — and they came. The doctrine in that verse is larger than the geography. God governs the pagan nations as directly as He governs Israel; He raises up the Mede against Babylon exactly as He raised Babylon against Jerusalem, and neither instrument knows whose hand it is in. Isaiah says it plainly of Cyrus: “I girded thee, though thou hast not known me” (Isa 45:5). Ashkenaz belongs to that theme. A remote descendant of Japheth, listed in a genealogy long before there was a Babylon to punish, is on file in heaven as part of the answer to the prayers of a captive people.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Ashkenaz; in sacred geography he is the eldest son of Gomer, and the head of a northern kingdom named by Jeremiah.

expand to see more

ASHKENAZ, n. The first named son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth.

His brethren were Riphath and Togarmah, heads likewise of northern nations.

Jeremiah summons the kingdom of Ashchenaz, with Ararat and Minni, against Babylon.

The spelling varies between Ashkenaz and Ashchenaz in the English text, following the Hebrew.

The nation is reckoned among the peoples of the north in the prophetic writings.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:3 — "And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah."

1Ch 1:6 — "And the sons of Gomer; Ashchenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah."

Jer 51:27 — "Set ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough caterpillers."

Gen 10:2 — "The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras."

Modern Corruption

The name has been borrowed for a later ethnic label and then read backward into Genesis; and the summoning of pagan armies is softened into God merely permitting what men decide.

expand to see more

A medieval usage attached the name Ashkenaz to the Jewish communities of the Rhineland, and from there it became a standing ethnic term. That later borrowing tells us nothing whatever about the son of Gomer, yet it is regularly read back into Genesis 10 to construct racial genealogies for modern peoples — sometimes innocently, sometimes to serve theories that deny the ancestry of actual Jews. The dictionary rejects the whole procedure. Genesis 10 assigns nations as they stood in Moses' day; it is not a chart of modern ethnicity, and no modern people can claim or be denied its identity from a name adopted three thousand years later.

The second corruption is doctrinal and far more common. Jeremiah does not say that God foresaw the northern kingdoms would attack Babylon; he says God calls them together and appoints a captain over them. That is government, not observation. The instinct to soften it — to say God permits, allows, or works around the free choices of nations — comes from a doctrine of providence too small for the text. Scripture is unembarrassed: “The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will” (Pro 21:1). The same sovereignty that summons Ashchenaz against Babylon delivered up the Lord Jesus “by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God” (Act 2:23), and in both cases the men who acted did what their own hearts chose and were justly answerable for it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'Ashkenaz (H813), Ashkenaz; Gomer (H1586), Gomer; mamlakah (H4467), kingdom; qara' (H7121), to call, summon; nes (H5251), standard, banner.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'Ashkenaz (H813) — Ashkenaz; eldest son of Gomer, and the kingdom named from him.

Hebrew Gomer (H1586) — Gomer; his father, the firstborn of Japheth.

Hebrew mamlakah (H4467) — kingdom, realm; what Ashchenaz has become by Jeremiah's day.

Hebrew qara' (H7121) — to call, proclaim, summon; God's act toward the northern armies.

Hebrew nes (H5251) — standard, ensign, signal-pole; set up in the land to muster the nations.

Usage

"“The kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz” — three pagan armies mustered by name."

"“Appoint a captain against her” — the LORD commissions officers in armies that do not know Him."

"A grandson of Japheth on file as an instrument of judgment centuries before the judgment."
